title: Runner-Up Score

examples.explanation: The highest score is 92. The next highest different score is 88.
Everyone tied, so there is no runner-up score.

approaches.name: one pass tracking the top two distinct values

steps.title: Clarify the input
steps.description: Confirms that ties don't count as a second place and what to return when there's no runner-up.
look_for: asks whether duplicates of the top score count
mentions the empty list or a single score
hints: Before you start, is there anything about ties you'd want to confirm?
If two players share the top score, is the second of them the runner-up?
Pin down that the runner-up must be a different score, and what the answer is when none exists.

steps.title: Track the top two in one pass
steps.description: Keeps the best and second-best distinct scores while scanning once.
look_for: updates both when a new best appears
hints: Look at what you keep track of as you scan.
When a new highest score arrives, what happens to the old highest?
Keep a best and a second-best; a new best pushes the old best down to second.

steps.title: Ignore copies of the top score
steps.description: Doesn't let a repeat of the current best become the second-best.
look_for: uses a strict comparison against the best
tests a list with a tied top score
hints: Try your code on a list where the top score appears twice.
Should a second copy of the best score ever become the runner-up?
Only take a score as second-best if it's strictly below the best.

steps.title: Start from a safe value
steps.description: Initializes so that 0 can be a real runner-up and -1 comes back when there isn't one.
hints: Look at the values your variables start with.
If every score is the same, what does your function give back right now?
Start both trackers below any valid score, like -1, so 'no runner-up' and 0 stay different.

edge_cases.description: the top score comes after the runner-up

common_mistakes.description: sorts and takes the second-to-last element
forgets to move the old best down to second place when a new best arrives

wrap_up_questions: What are the time and space complexity?
How would you change this to return the k-th highest distinct score?

origin_note: Original. Pattern: one pass tracking the top two distinct values.
